findings.title: Grok response-size amplification can still strand a native captured answer
findings.verification_status: Static causal trace only; payload not executed
findings.summary: A genuine, in-budget Grok question can produce an over-budget wire answer even when the tiny submitted values satisfy the shared validator. The native editor captures the second F5 before the concrete encoder checks the expanded response. Rejection leaves canonical state pending but local captured set, so edits and F7 are refused under the unchanged original grant. This preserves authority and responder safety but violates deliberate native correction/cancellation availability.

locations.role: Question text accepted by type/nonempty/uniqueness, without a wire-response representability bound
Original question retained as canonical field title
Original question duplicated as answers and annotations map keys
Shared validation checks submitted values/schema/Other notes but not expanded Grok response size
Concrete expanded frame rejected above FRAME
Shared validation followed by two-step capture before daemon admission

Capture cleared only for synchronous local enqueue rejection
Asynchronous capacity-exceeded error keeps control and does not return the captured envelope

source_to_failure_trace: The owned adapter submits _x.ai/ask_user_question using the exact current session/tool/RPC, mode default, one question consisting of 600000 ASCII Q characters, multiSelect false, and one short option {label:Zero, description:No adjustment}.

[INFERENCE from exact lengths and source, not run] The inbound JSON is about 600 KB and therefore below FRAME=1048576. grok::form accepts one distinct nonempty question and a short option, injects Other plus q0_notes, and copies question text once into the schema title. parse_form/schema validation accepts that title string; canonical/native interaction accounting is below 4 MiB.

The human chooses Other and supplies notes 7. The values object {q0:Other,q0_notes:7-as-string} is tiny, satisfies required fields/types/offered choice and the repaired nonempty-notes predicate, and passes native F5 review.

Second F5 captures the action locally; this small envelope fits the native RPC queue. The daemon uses the original current grant and exact tuple, enters the authority-to-broker admission transaction, and validates those same values.

grok::response inserts the entire 600000-byte question as a key in answers and again as a key in annotations because notes are present. The two ASCII keys alone occupy 1200000 bytes, exceeding the 1048576-byte outgoing frame ceiling independently of envelope overhead.
encode returns capacity-exceeded before broker selection/work/call-ID publication. No wire response or invented answer is sent; the original interaction/responder remains pending.

NativeControl reports asynchronous capacity-exceeded without invalidating the unchanged grant. The top-level TUI only invokes restore_unqueued for a synchronous local submit failure. AgentView sync sees the same binding, revision and pending canonical disposition and retains captured.

Interaction::editable refuses all later native edits/F5/F7 while captured is Some. Escaping through a different authority, the API, or closing/reopening is not deliberate correction/cancellation on the retained native grant. No security boundary is crossed.

evidence.label: Admission controls do not bound question title length below the frame budget
evidence.explanation: grok::form checks nonempty question text, duplicate texts, question/option counts, exact primitive types, modes and IDs; validate_form_schema permits string title annotations without a serialized-response-size bound.

evidence.label: Annotated reply repeats the large ingress key
evidence.explanation: Even minimal nonempty Other notes create annotations. The full original question is copied as a second map key; this is required by the implemented concrete wire representation, not speculative resource pressure.

evidence.label: Post-capture encoding rejects before canonical selection
evidence.explanation: encode serializes the entire response and then enforces FRAME. Broker commit performs this fallible encoding before the no-fallible-publication section. The responder remains safely pending while local capture has already happened.

evidence.label: The native editor cannot intentionally recover with the same grant
evidence.explanation: capture records call_id; editable rejects captured; restore_unqueued is only called on synchronous local enqueue rejection. The asynchronous error branch and unchanged pending projection do not clear capture.

findings.impact: A permitted, bounded Grok interaction can enter a native state that can neither be accepted nor deliberately corrected/cancelled using that original grant, despite the canonical responder remaining available. The API can still cancel; no false canonical answer, arbitrary execution, authority bypass or secret exposure is claimed.
findings.remediation: Validate concrete serialized Grok response representability before native capture, with a shared representation-aware budget check, or reject at ingress question/annotation expansions that cannot fit the existing frame contract. Preserve pending/editable/F7 behavior on validation failure and the original tuple/grant; do not implement replay or late authority substitution. Add a deterministic original-RPC/native case for an in-budget long question whose annotated reply would exceed FRAME.
findings.why_not_security: General DoS/resource consumption is excluded by the required security skill, and no independent security exploit path is established. This finding is reported solely as a concrete operational validation/capture defect.

checklist.assessment: Read the actual 12-line conventions and required execution amendment. The repair reuses existing flat validation and the private Grok codec without a new provider framework, persistence layer or dependency.

Closed Target decoding, explicit session_id including null, and Instance::exact compare kind/id/instance/connection/session; updates, forms and permissions validate the live session. No late lookup substitutes a newly opened instance.

Daemon preauthorization is not the final gate: Authority::admit_acp rechecks live reference/controller/generation while holding the target lock, then broker commit rechecks captured generation and exact tuple. Revocation and commit share that target ordering point.

pending_interaction requires exact ID/revision/kind/state and responder mapping. All fallible validation/encoding/capacity checks precede selection/work/call publication; a losing prepared action cannot add accepted history or write a second response.

Force grants control through the authority state machine without broker cancellation or process signals. Writer consumes immutable accepted records without checking the later owner; original work/RPC/controller identities remain retained.

checklist.area: Ordinary pending cancellation and no replay
checklist.assessment: Ordinary ownership claim state remains separate from session/cancel and ACP work. Registry cancellation/yield/recovery tests exercise granting nobody and retained original calls; ACP writer does not rebind/replay accepted records when ownership changes.

Conditional claims require an external requester and a live original attachment owner; eligibility uses original view/activity and the existing reservation state machine. No ACP-specific automatic reacquisition policy is introduced.

Possession of a borrowed control capability can authorize an action but cannot manufacture native activity/consent. View reporting checks the original live connection, and admit_acp records activity only for is_original_native.

The extension requires known mode, tool identity, exact session through parse_form, distinct question texts/option labels, bounded question/option counts, well-typed descriptions/previews, and nonambiguous nullable multiselect flags. Unknown extensions remain method-not-found; malformed supported requests become invalid-params without fabricated answers.

Required/optional distinction, false/zero/empty/unset, types, Unicode lengths, finite numeric/i64 bounds, enum intersection and distinct offered multiselect selections are checked. Unsupported controls/constraints reject explicitly; pattern/format limitations are retained and documented, not certified.

checklist.area: Repaired Other notes and unsupported decline
checklist.assessment: The moved rule runs in native values() before review/capture and again at broker admission. Scalar Other and any array containing Other require notes of string type with nonempty contents; omitted/null/number/boolean/array/empty notes cannot pass. Without grok_notes_key metadata the extra conditional is inactive. Grok decline errors before publication; UI F6 sends nothing when not offered.

checklist.area: Concrete response representability before native capture
checklist.assessment: Flat answer validation does not establish that the concrete Grok response fits FRAME. Full question keys can be repeated in annotations; a legal ~600-KB question plus tiny Other notes yields a >1.2-MB reply rejected after native capture. Unchanged canonical pending state does not make that native draft editable/F7-cancellable.

checklist.area: Original wire responder and ID reuse
checklist.assessment: Interaction wire_id and exact parent scope survive handoff and parent completion. Responder write stamps distinguish not-finished/written/failed; Arc identity prevents late writer bookkeeping from deleting a fresh reused responder. Typed numeric/string RPC IDs do not alias.

Interrupt addresses the exact current foreground prompt and reserves session/cancel plus all applicable pending form/permission responses before commit. Selected interactions are not answered twice. Late applicable requests become selected/nonselectable with Cancel/Cancelled, or fail explicitly before publication if capacity is unavailable.

Notification/write success is delivery evidence, not confirmed interruption or tool death. Original prompt responses supply stop reason; EOF/error closes genuinely unresolved work as unknown without overwriting completed original responses. Permission reject_once returning cancelled is distinct from issuing session/cancel.

checklist.area: Startup, close and shutdown lifetime races
checklist.assessment: Reservation/initial control precede async launch publication. AcpLifetime serializes startup/apply against end, and late publication requires the target still live. Close atomically ends authority; child/process cleanup and joins occur outside admission locks. Failed-open rollback requires empty, ended, complete cleanup.

Mutation/application ordering is target authority then broker state. Snapshot copies ACP descriptors before leaving topology lock and projecting broker/ownership metadata. Spawn, blocking write, process probes/termination and joins are outside those locks. No broker-state-to-authority/topology cycle was found in the inspected paths.

checklist.area: Hostile ingress framing and FIFO budgets
checklist.assessment: read_frame checks length before extending and rejects partial EOF. Reader reserves maximum accumulation bytes/count before reading; in-flight frames remain charged through ordered apply. Malformed UTF-8/JSON, oversize/flood/queue failure degrades the exact instance rather than silently dropping messages and claiming continuity.

Count and byte limits include queued/in-flight output; RPC registration precedes enqueue. Duplicate lifetime call-ID tombstones survive history eviction with a reserved final close admission. Capacity rejection precedes canonical publication; the representability/UI consequence is separately counted only in item12.

Transcript, completed work and interaction history use explicit caps/gap counters. Pending/responding interactions are not evicted to manufacture capacity; completed content can be trimmed. Native caches have explicit bounded accounting and incremental cursors, not an unbounded full-history copy per frame.

checklist.area: Independent cancellation of held pipe I/O
checklist.assessment: Original files are nonblocking and shared through one owner. Poll waits include the sticky wake socket; stop uses ConnectionAborted rather than retryable Interrupted. A completed syscall retains its actual result. Workers are joined, not detached, even if an escaped process retains endpoints.

checklist.area: Cleanup truth and retained resource charge
checklist.assessment: Idle/early-return workers cannot erase endpoint evidence: the owner retains all original handles through known-tree cleanup and joins, probes every endpoint, then drops descriptors before finish. Missing/held/unclassifiable endpoints and capture failure stay failed/incomplete and charged. Orphan termination is not falsely claimed.

checklist.area: Owned process identity and signal scope
checklist.assessment: ProcessTree captures the owned session leader and start identity, discovers descendants/session members only while identities still match, and birth-checks signals. Uncaptured fallback signals the still-unreaped direct child/group then waits; it does not reuse killpg after reap. No unrelated PID or escaped unknown holder is deliberately signalled.

checklist.area: Host terminal injection and native input isolation
checklist.assessment: ACP text is ratatui display data; control/escape/bidi/line-format characters are neutralized in broker content and native rendering/chrome. Active ACP events are consumed, even on None, rather than falling through to raw PTY input. Terminal-only operations explicitly reject ACP IDs/kinds.

checklist.area: Draft authority fencing and synchronous queue rejection
checklist.assessment: First edit captures the original complete tuple/grant; changed identity/authority discards the draft. Native control forwards the captured envelope unchanged, never substitutes a current token, and only synchronous local enqueue rejection restores an original unqueued draft for deliberate resubmission. The separate asynchronous representability defect is item12, not a second authority issue.

Authentication requires an explicit advertised agent method; unsupported auth kinds do not become usable agent auth. Permission responses use exact offered IDs/kinds, with no synthetic allow or dismissal-to-deny. URL/fs/terminal delegation is unadvertised, and unknown service requests get errors rather than auto-opening resources.

Default projections/events expose bounded identities/state rather than schema/values/transcript. Content is explicit local inspection; error text/data and stderr are not projected as raw provider diagnostics. Synthetic privacy oracles inspect snapshot/events/default inspect for private markers. Same-user socket access is the trust boundary, not a multiuser content ACL.

Production uses absolute operator-selected executable argv and direct Command args/current_dir, not remote shell interpolation. Adapter-owned tools are not sandboxed by amux. Live-only shell effects use a fixed command, reject apostrophes in the private configured cwd and require exact offered path/command before selecting permission; no production command-injection path was established.

Tests use actual isolated daemon/stdio/controlling-PTY consumers, observable arithmetic and exact original wire responses, rendered readiness and cleanup assertions before fallback. Fast: bounded local waits/fixture workload, no provider in default suite. Independent: unique private roots/env. Repeatable: predicates/barriers rather than sleep-as-proof. Self-validating: exact tuple/RPC/effects/absence. Timely: supplied test-only RED1707 preceded the local validation repair. New representability coverage is requested in the finding, not claimed present.

The ignored entry requires explicit config and exact Codex/Grok IDs/four-prompt approval/private fresh effect roots. Observer forwards accepted bytes unchanged, checks model/effort, and keeps a cumulative prompt budget; no hard-USD/subrequest guarantee follows. Parent real OAuth1659 belongs to round4, not the repaired source; current native/CLI/full artifacts prove local paths only.

Concrete broker/codec/editor boundaries have useful depth and reuse existing authority/validation/cleanup conventions. No new generic provider abstraction, public signature, compatibility shim or dependency is introduced by the reported repair. Long Method in causal E2E traces is an acknowledged tradeoff, not a line-count finding. No actionable Feature Envy, Data Clumps, Message Chains or Middle Man was established.
